name: נַפְתָּלִי
summary: Jacob’s sixth son, the second born to him by Bilhah, Rachel’s maid, and the tribe that came from him, which camped north of the tabernacle in Dan’s camp and set out last of all from Sinai under Ahira son of Enan (Num 2:29; 10:27). Rachel named him from the root’s niphal and its noun: “נַפְתּוּלֵי אֱלֹהִים נִפְתַּלְתִּי, wrestlings of God I have wrestled with my sister, and I have prevailed” (Gen 30:8). The name is that noun with the ending -î, “my wrestling”. Barak of Kedesh-naphtali led the tribe with Zebulun against Sisera (Jdg 4:6, 10; 5:18), and Isaiah’s “land of Naphtali” that sees a great light is fulfilled, Matthew says, when Jesus comes to live at Capernaum in the borders of Zebulun and Naphtali (Isa 8:23–9:1; Mat 4:13–16).

evidence.note: “With wrestlings of God I have wrestled (נִפְתַּלְתִּי) with my sister, and I have prevailed; and she called his name נַפְתָּלִי.”
The sons of Bilhah, Rachel’s maid: Dan and Naphtali.
The sons of Naphtali: Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer and Shillem.
Jacob’s blessing: “Naphtali is a hind let loose; he gives words of beauty.”
For Naphtali, Ahira son of Enan.
Beside Dan and Asher on the north side, under Ahira son of Enan.
“Over the host of the tribe of the sons of Naphtali, Ahira son of Enan”: the last tribe to set out, in the camp of Dan.
Moses: “Naphtali, satisfied with favour and full of the blessing of Yahweh, possess the sea and the south.”
Deborah calls Barak from Kedesh-naphtali to take ten thousand men of Naphtali and Zebulun to Mount Tabor.
“Zebulun was a people that risked their lives to the death, and Naphtali, on the heights of the field.”
Hiram the bronze-worker, son of a widow of the tribe of Naphtali.
Tiglath-pileser takes all the land of Naphtali and carries its people captive to Assyria.
“He brought contempt on the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, but afterward he has made glorious the way of the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations.”
Jesus lives at Capernaum “in the borders of Zebulun and Νεφθαλείμ”, fulfilling Isaiah’s word.
Naphtali’s portion in Ezekiel’s land, between Asher and Manasseh.
One of the city’s west gates, the gate of Naphtali.
Of the tribe of Νεφθαλείμ twelve thousand were sealed.

note: Takes q.ec.ae (51 tokens), which also counts the tribe and its land (Jos 19:32–39; 1Ki 15:20); TIPNR has the man Naphtali@Gen.30.8, and Kedesh-naphtali is a place record (Kedesh@Jos.12.22), not tagged here. The Septuagint and New Testament spell it Νεφθαλείμ. The ending -î is read as “my” from Rachel’s first-person verb (נִפְתַּלְתִּי); it could also be the adjectival -î, “one of wrestling”.
